title: Reducing Buyer Search Costs: Implications for Electronic Marketplaces
book_use: Ch 1-3; Ch 6; Ch 9; Ch 23 search costs and electronic intermediaries; Notes: Foundational model of how electronic marketplaces reduce buyer search costs; does not imply complete price convergence.

author_or_institution: Erik Brynjolfsson and Michael D. Smith
title: Frictionless Commerce? A Comparison of Internet and Conventional Retailers
book_use: Ch 2; Ch 6; Ch 23 historical counterexample to frictionless-market claims; Notes: Finds lower online friction alongside meaningful price dispersion and persistent brand/trust effects in the studied markets.

title: Buy it in ChatGPT: Instant Checkout and the Agentic Commerce Protocol
book_use: Ch 1; Ch 4-5; Ch 7; Ch 14-15 live agentic checkout infrastructure; Notes: Establishes a real 2025 agentic-commerce deployment; vendor source, so adoption and welfare claims require independent evidence.

title: Introducing our agentic commerce solutions
book_use: Ch 1; Ch 4-5; Ch 12; Ch 15 ACP payments and merchant control; Notes: Describes Stripe's work with OpenAI on ACP and the trust/permission assumptions changed by agentic checkout.

title: Under the Hood: Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP)
book_use: Ch 5; Ch 14-15; Ch 18; Ch 23 interoperability and machine-readable commerce; Notes: Describes UCP as an open-source commerce standard spanning consumer surfaces, businesses, payments, APIs, A2A and MCP.

title: Powering AI commerce with the new Agent Payments Protocol (AP2)
book_use: Ch 4; Ch 12; Ch 16; Ch 19; Ch 23 delegated authority and payment mandates; Notes: Useful for verifiable intent and payment-agnostic agent authorization; protocol evolution should be refreshed in later editions.

title: The agentic commerce platform: Shopify connects any merchant to every AI conversation
book_use: Ch 5; Ch 14-15; Ch 18 merchant catalogs and agentic channels; Notes: Describes UCP, Agentic Storefronts and opening Shopify Catalog to non-Shopify brands; commercial claims should be treated as vendor evidence.

title: Selling everything, everywhere, all at once: Spring '26 Edition
book_use: Ch 5; Ch 15; Ch 18 structured product data and catalog distribution; Notes: Reports merchant-facing Catalog/UCP capabilities and a vendor-reported conversion advantage for structured catalog data.

title: Introducing Shopify Agentic Storefronts
book_use: Ch 5; Ch 7; Ch 14-15 in-conversation shopping surfaces; Notes: Supports the claim that merchant discovery and checkout are moving into AI conversations.

title: Buy for Me button on Amazon Shopping app
book_use: Ch 1; Ch 5; Ch 14 agentic purchasing across merchant boundaries; Notes: Beta deployment in which Amazon's app can complete purchases on participating external brand sites; do not generalize beta usage to mass adoption.

title: Mastercard unveils Agent Pay
book_use: Ch 4; Ch 12-13; Ch 16; Ch 19; Ch 21 delegated payment identity and tokenization; Notes: Describes Agentic Tokens and consumer/business use cases; vendor vision is evidence of infrastructure investment, not forecast validation.

title: Ushering in the intelligence layer
book_use: Ch 4; Ch 12; Ch 16; Ch 21; Ch 23 trust, services, agentic commerce; Notes: Useful for payments/trust/service architecture and industry direction.

title: Agent Pay for Machines
book_use: Ch 16; Ch 23 machine-to-machine commerce and microtransactions; Notes: Establishes a concrete machine-payment product category; long-run transaction volume is speculative.

title: Surveillance Pricing Study Indicates Wide Range of Personal Data Used to Set Individualized Consumer Prices
book_use: Ch 8; Ch 16 personalized pricing and information asymmetry; Notes: Initial 6(b) study findings on intermediary capabilities and data inputs; examples include hypothetical illustrations and should not be described as universal retailer practice.

title: Dark commercial patterns
book_use: Ch 7; Ch 11; Ch 17 consumer manipulation and interface design; Notes: Defines and synthesizes evidence on digital choice architectures that steer or manipulate consumers.

title: Stronger consumer protections needed to address current and emerging harms consumers face online
book_use: Ch 11; Ch 17 prevalence and consumer harm from dark patterns; Notes: Summarizes a 35,000+ respondent survey across 20 countries; use for scale and prevalence, not causal estimates of each practice.

title: FTC v. Uber Technologies, Inc.
book_use: Ch 11 recurring billing and cancellation friction; Notes: Pending litigation as of May 2026 alleging subscription billing and cancellation violations; allegations are not findings of liability.

title: Semiannual Federal Court Litigation Status Report (December 2025)
book_use: Ch 11 counterevidence on regulatory durability; Notes: Records the July 8 2025 appellate decision vacating the FTC click-to-cancel rule; important correction to outdated descriptions of the rule as operative federal law.

title: World Trade Report 2025: Making trade and AI work together to the benefit of all
book_use: Ch 18; Ch 23 AI, trade costs, inclusion and policy; Notes: Primary global-trade source; stresses both reduced trade costs and uneven access to infrastructure and skills.

author_or_institution: World Trade Organization and International Chamber of Commerce
title: business survey on AI use in trade
book_use: Ch 18 firm-size and income-country adoption gaps; Notes: Survey of 158 firms; useful directional evidence but not representative of all global firms.

title: Digital Progress and Trends Report 2025: Strengthening AI Foundations
book_use: Ch 18; Ch 23 connectivity, compute, context and competency gaps; Notes: Global development source for uneven AI foundations and digital participation; later editions should refresh statistics.

title: Strengthening AI Foundations: Emerging Opportunities for Developing Countries
book_use: Ch 18 current figures on connectivity, compute and skills; Notes: Accessible companion to DPTR 2025 with current distributional statistics.

title: Global Findex Database 2025
book_use: Ch 13; Ch 18; Ch 21 digital payments, accounts, mobile ownership and inclusion; Notes: Based on nationally representative surveys across 141 economies conducted in 2024; useful for payment access and digital inclusion.

title: Digital Markets Act Developer Portal — Interoperability
book_use: Ch 14; Ch 19; Ch 23 platform contestability and interoperability; Notes: Current EU precedent for requiring gatekeeper interoperability; not a claim that future agent services automatically fall under identical obligations.

title: DMA smartphone interoperability and data portability case studies
book_use: Ch 19 credible exit, portability and switching costs; Notes: Concrete 2026 examples of portability/interoperability remedies in mobile ecosystems.

title: DMA Review Q&A
book_use: Ch 14; Ch 19; Ch 23 evolving gatekeeper policy; Notes: Provides current Commission assessment of DMA contestability, portability and implementation challenges.

title: Consumer policy and digital technologies
book_use: Ch 7; Ch 11-12; Ch 17; Ch 20-21 consumer protection across data, reviews, payments and dark patterns; Notes: Useful overview of current consumer-policy problem areas; prefer underlying studies for specific quantitative claims.

title: The global internet gap: What the data tells us
book_use: Ch 18 internet-access constraints and global participation; Notes: Reports that billions remain offline and highlights sharp income-country gaps; use as a current-access snapshot.

title: World Development Report 2026 press release: AI Offers Lifeline to Developing Economies in an Era of Weak Growth
book_use: Ch 18; Ch 23 current development constraints and opportunity; Notes: Fresh 2026 framing of power, connectivity, skills and institutional quality as conditions for broad AI gains; the full report should replace the press summary in a later research pass.

author_or_institution: National Retail Federation and Happy Returns
title: 2025 Retail Returns Landscape
book_use: Ch 20 return volume, online return rates, consumer expectations and fraud; Notes: Survey-based industry estimates project $849.9B of returns and a 19.3% online return rate; useful for scale, not an official national ledger.

title: Ecodesign for Sustainable Products Regulation
book_use: Ch 20 repairability, lifecycle product information and digital product passports; Notes: Provides EU policy direction for product durability, circularity and digital product information; implementation is phased and product-specific.

title: The Buy Now, Pay Later Market
book_use: Ch 21 BNPL market growth, loan volume and borrower obligations; Notes: Uses data from six large BNPL firms for 2022-2023; market structure and regulation continue to evolve.

title: Consumer Use of Buy Now, Pay Later and Other Unsecured Debt
book_use: Ch 13; Ch 21 simultaneous BNPL loans, borrower credit profiles and fragmented debt; Notes: Matched provider and de-identified credit-record study; supports fragmentation claims without implying BNPL is inherently harmful.

title: Community Choice Aggregation
book_use: Ch 22 demand aggregation and collective purchasing precedent; Notes: Shows local governments aggregating electricity demand under enabling state law; useful as a concrete precedent, not a general template for every market.

title: Buying Data from Consumers
book_use: Ch 21 telematics, proprietary data, portability and consumer welfare counterevidence; Notes: Models and documents how consumer monitoring can improve behavior and welfare while proprietary data can also create switching and incentive tradeoffs.

title: Ephraim Leibtag, Andrew Leicester and Aviv Nevo, Consumer Shopping Behavior: How Much Do Consumers Save?
book_use: Ch 22 household purchasing behavior, bulk buying and outlet choice; Notes: Empirical review of savings from sales, bulk purchasing, generic brands and outlet choice; useful background for organized demand rather than evidence about future agent coalitions.

title: AI agents for cash management in payment systems
book_use: Ch 13 household-treasury analogy for sequencing liquidity obligations under constraints; Notes: Prompt-based experiments test a reasoning model on simulated intraday liquidity management in wholesale payments; useful as a constrained analogy, not evidence that consumer agents should autonomously control household finances.

title: Trusted Agent Protocol
book_use: Ch 4; Ch 12; Ch 16 merchant recognition, agent identity and delegated payment trust; Notes: Defines mechanisms for merchants to distinguish approved commerce agents from malicious bots and link agent, consumer/device identity and payment information; vendor protocol evidence, not adoption evidence.

title: FIDO Alliance to Develop Standards for Trusted AI Agent Interactions
book_use: Ch 12 agent authentication, authorization and interoperable agentic payment frameworks; Notes: Documents formation of the Agentic Authentication Technical Working Group and standards work drawing on AP2 and Mastercard Verifiable Intent; specifications are still developing.

title: Introducing the Machine Payments Protocol
book_use: Ch 12; Ch 16; Ch 23 machine-to-machine payments and software buying digital services; Notes: Describes the open Machine Payments Protocol co-authored by Stripe and Tempo for agent-native payments; proves infrastructure availability, not long-run transaction volume.

title: Competition and consumer policy in digital markets
book_use: Ch 14; Ch 19; Ch 23 consumer agency, platform gatekeeping and overlap between competition and consumer protection; Notes: Explicitly discusses agentic AI as potentially expanding or constraining consumer agency and creating new transparency, intermediation and self-preferencing concerns; policy analysis rather than observed long-run market effects.

title: Rule on Unfair or Deceptive Fees and 2025 compliance guidance
book_use: Ch 8 total-price disclosure, mandatory fees and machine-comparable offers; Notes: Effective May 12 2025 for live-event tickets and short-term lodging. Requires prominent upfront total prices including mandatory calculable fees while allowing limited exclusions and dynamic pricing; scope should not be generalized to all consumer markets.

title: U.S. and Plaintiff States v. RealPage, Inc. case materials
book_use: Ch 8 algorithmic pricing, competitively sensitive data and independent pricing; Notes: Case record includes the RealPage proposed settlement in November 2025, Greystar final judgment in March 2026 and Willow Bridge proposed settlement in July 2026. Use for the distinction between ordinary dynamic pricing and alleged coordination through shared competitive data; settlements are case-specific and not a blanket rule against pricing software.

title: IFRS 15 Revenue from Contracts with Customers — unexercised customer rights
book_use: Ch 10 breakage and the economics of expected non-redemption; Notes: Paragraphs B44-B47 address customer prepayments and unexercised rights commonly called breakage. Used narrowly to show that expected nonuse can be material to revenue accounting, not to claim every loyalty program follows identical economics.

title: Local Number Portability consumer and implementation materials
book_use: Ch 10 portability as a competition precedent for lowering a specific switching cost; Notes: FCC guidance confirms consumers can generally keep an existing number when switching providers within the same geographic area. Used as a limited analogy for separability of accumulated consumer context, not as a claim that agent memory is technically equivalent to a phone number.

title: Negative Option Rule Advance Notice of Proposed Rulemaking
book_use: Ch 11 post-vacatur negative-option policy, complaint rates and institutional latency; Notes: March 2026 ANPR records the July 2025 Eighth Circuit vacatur of the amended rule and reports negative-option complaints rising from at least 33 per day in late 2020 to more than 90 per day in 2025. Rulemaking is ongoing; figures are FTC complaint data, not a population prevalence estimate.

title: Overdraft and Nonsufficient Fund Fees: Insights from the Making Ends Meet Survey and Consumer Credit Panel
book_use: Ch 13 liquidity constraints, overdraft exposure and the limits of optimization; Notes: Combines the CFPB Making Ends Meet survey with credit-bureau data and finds greater financial vulnerability among frequent overdraft/NSF households. Used to distinguish avoidable timing errors from underlying resource constraints; U.S.-specific evidence, not a universal household-finance law.
